title: Bengaluru Landlord Security Deposit Withheld

missing_proof_needed: Proof of security deposit payment (bank transaction receipt/UPI/cheque)
Move-in and move-out inspection photos/videos or handover email confirmation
Written communication (WhatsApp/Email) showing notice given and demand for refund
case_summary.raw_story: I vacated my 2BHK flat in HSR Layout, Bengaluru on October 31st after giving 1 month notice as per agreement. I paid ₹65,000 deposit via Google Pay in 2023. The landlord inspected the house and confirmed everything was fine on WhatsApp. Now it's been over 25 days and he is refusing to return my deposit, saying he needs ₹40,000 for full house repainting and deep cleaning, but the house only had normal wear and tear. He is not answering my calls now.

legal_standing_and_options.standing: Strong Prima Facie Case under Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Section 108) & State Rent Control Acts / Model Tenancy Act
legal_standing_and_options.plain_explanation: Under Indian law, the other party cannot arbitrarily withhold your money without documented justification. You have a strong legal right to seek full refund of ₹65,000.
key_principles: A landlord cannot arbitrarily deduct from a security deposit without providing itemized repair bills for damage beyond normal wear and tear.
Normal wear and tear (e.g., minor paint fading, routine aging) is the landlord's responsibility, not the tenant's.
Deposit must be returned within the notice period or 30 days of handing over vacant possession unless the lease deed specifies otherwise.
Remedies: (1) Written formal demand notice via registered post/email, (2) Approach Rent Authority / Rent Tribunal or Civil Court for summary recovery.
options: Step 1: Send a Formal Written Demand Notice giving 15 clear days to settle.
Step 2: File a free pre-litigation grievance on government portals (e.g., National Consumer Helpline 1915 or State Labour Portal).
Step 3: If unresponsive, escalate to the appropriate statutory forum (District Consumer Commission via e-Daakhil or Rent Authority).

title: E-Commerce Refusal to Refund Damaged Appliance

missing_proof_needed: Photographs / unboxing video of damaged or wrong product
Chat transcripts or customer service ticket history
case_summary.raw_story: I ordered a semi-automatic washing machine for ₹18,499 from QuickMart on 5th Nov. When delivery arrived on 8th Nov, the motor drum was badly dented and making loud grinding noises. I immediately created a return request with photos within 2 hours. Customer service closed the ticket saying 'Damage not reported at delivery time'. I escalated via email three times with unboxing video, but they keep sending automated rejection emails.

legal_standing_and_options.standing: Strong Prima Facie Case under Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Sections 2(7), 2(47), 35, 84-86) & E-Commerce Rules 2020
legal_standing_and_options.plain_explanation: Under Indian law, the other party cannot arbitrarily withhold your money without documented justification. You have a strong legal right to seek full refund of ₹18,499.
key_principles: Consumer Protection Act 2019 Section 2(7) protects anyone buying goods/services online or offline.
Unfair Trade Practice under Section 2(47): Refusing legitimate refund or delivering defective goods contrary to merchant terms.
Section 35: Filing complaint before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (DCDRC) for claims up to ₹50 Lakhs (e-Daakhil portal).
National Consumer Helpline (NCH - 1915 or consumerhelpline.gov.in) provides free pre-litigation grievance mediation.

title: Unpaid Salary and Relieving Letter Withheld by Employer

missing_proof_needed: Salary slips / Bank statement showing prior monthly credits
Resignation letter and written acceptance / Relieving email
case_summary.raw_story: I worked as a frontend engineer at Apex Tech Solutions Pvt Ltd in Gurugram for 1.5 years. I submitted my resignation on September 1st and served my full 30-day notice period till September 30th with handover done. My company has not paid my September salary (₹60,000) and August arrears (₹45,000), total ₹1,05,000. HR is not releasing my relieving letter or experience certificate, claiming the client project had bugs. My new employer is threatening to revoke my offer if I don't submit relieving letter.

legal_standing_and_options.standing: Strong Prima Facie Case under Payment of Wages Act, 1936 & State Shops and Commercial Establishments Act
legal_standing_and_options.plain_explanation: Under Indian law, the other party cannot arbitrarily withhold your money without documented justification. You have a strong legal right to seek full refund of ₹1,05,000.
key_principles: Wages must be paid by the 7th or 10th of the succeeding month.
Full and final settlement (F&F) including unpaid salary, encashable leave, and bonus must generally be settled within 30–45 days of relieving.
An employer cannot arbitrarily withhold earned wages even if a dispute regarding notice period exists without formal inquiry.

Remedies: (1) Formal Legal Demand Notice giving 15 days, (2) Grievance to the Labour Commissioner under State Shops & Establishments Act, (3) NCLT insolvency application for corporate defaults exceeding statutory thresholds.

title: Dubious Recovery Agent Police Arrest Threat (Escalation Case)

case_summary.raw_story: A man claiming to be Inspector Rathore from Crime Branch called me and sent a PDF on WhatsApp with a fake police seal, claiming an FIR has been lodged against me for non-payment of a ₹15,000 loan app debt and police will come to arrest me and my parents today if I don't transfer ₹25,000 immediately to a personal UPI ID.

legal_standing_and_options.standing: CRITICAL WARNING: Threat of arrest / Police impersonation detected.
legal_standing_and_options.plain_explanation: No legitimate police officer or court sends arrest warrants on WhatsApp or demands money via personal UPI IDs. This is an illegal intimidation/extortion attempt by rogue recovery agents or fraudsters.
options: DO NOT transfer any money to the personal UPI ID.
Save all screenshots, call recordings, and the PDF with fake seals.
Immediately file a cyber fraud report on https://cybercrime.gov.in or dial National Cyber Helpline 1930.
Consult a licensed criminal advocate immediately if they show up at your residence.

roleplay_counter_argument: Opposing Party: 'We have received your message. However, as per company policy, no further refund is entertainable.'
